== Research Notes ==
=== Huntingdon and Cambria family review — 17 October 2026 ===

Select John Glasgow of Sinking Valley ([[Glasgow-1549]]) as the possible working father of John S. Glasgow Jr. of Cambria ([[Glasgow-664]]), at 57% subjective confidence. The family account identifies a missing young son John, while the existing Cambria John supplies a compatible son-generation identity in the same central Pennsylvania settlement area. His reported 1777 Scottish birth would make him about three in 1781, just older than the attached Richard, reportedly born about 1778. The elder John’s estimated 1758 birth permits that generation; neither estimate is a recorded age. The younger man’s Jr. label is modest supporting context, not independent proof of his father’s name. The explicit son report, ordered childhood chronology and regional continuity together favour this particular household over a father chosen only by forename. The 57% assesses both the reliability of the contributed son report and the identification of that son with this later adult; it is not a statistical result or a confidence rating for the whole ancestral path.

The saved biography of John [[Glasgow-1549]] explicitly reports that he and Margaret Hunter sailed for America in 1781 with two young sons, Richard and John (2), and that William was born during the voyage. Its attached children include Richard, William, Matthew and Taylor Wilson, but no John. This is an overlooked, specific family attribution in a contributed account, not a newly discovered passenger list or inspected birth record. The underlying source of the travel and son statements is not identified. The separate will citation must not be presented as having proved those statements: its image could not be inspected in this review.

The freshly inspected 1790 Huntingdon transcription lists John Glasgo, page 116 line 7, with one male aged sixteen or more, five males under sixteen and one female. It gives no names or relationships for the younger people, and does not identify a township for this line. The reported John, Richard, William and Matthew could fit four of those boys, with one unidentified; Taylor Wilson’s reported 1798 birth is later than the return. That is a compatible household comparison, not evidence that those boys were the named sons or that this head was John-1549. Likewise the 1799 Allegheny Township election list may concern the older or younger John or another namesake. The 1820 Cambria locality is supportive regional context, not a continuous personal record from 1790. Keep every census and newspaper identity qualified separately.

Another unrecorded son John or a different Scottish immigrant remains possible. John [[Glasgow-3726]], reported born in Cumberland County in 1764 and later in Kentucky, is an older Pennsylvania comparison; his reported birthplace and chronology fit the two young emigrant sons less well, but unverified family dates are not absolute exclusions. John [[Glasgow-209]], reported born in County Londonderry in 1780 and later in Bakerstown, has a different Hugh/Blair parent account and locality history; these are substantive competing family circumstances, rather than proof that every missing John belongs here. The bounded catalogue comparison found no stronger central Pennsylvania John among the checked 1760s–1780s identities. The claimed Daill, Argyll birthplace of John-664 and the Glasgow-city origin in the elder family account remain unverified and are not equated or changed. Glasgow residence of the parents need not identify each child’s birthplace. No mother is selected: Margaret Hunter is the travelling wife in the account, which does not independently establish that she bore this John. No parentage is assigned to Samuel [[Glasgow-1984]] merely because his estimated age could fit the fifth boy. The older Richard [[Glasgow-1550]] attachment and its uncertain Scottish ancestry receive no new support. All existing spouses, children, dates and places remain unchanged; there is no merge, new person or live WikiTree save.

Inspect the cited Huntingdon will image 103 and adjacent continuation pages for John, the other named children, property descriptions and prior settlements. Trace the source behind the family account and inspect deeds, tax lists and any estate releases linking Sinking Valley to Allegheny/Cambria. Check the original 1790 and 1820 census pages and the basis of the younger John’s exact birthday and Daill birthplace. A named son in the will must still be identified with the Cambria adult; an omitted son is not by itself an exclusion. Keep the Scottish Richard/Ezekiel ancestry as a separate question.

=== Possible John Glasgow, Allegheny Township list in Huntingdon County context, 1799 ===
John Glasgow is named under Allegheny Township in a township-grouped list accompanying Huntingdon County election-meeting material.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/587806805/ The North American (Philadelphia), 1799-09-10, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1140587856/ Pennsylvania Weekly Telegraph (Oracle of Dauphin and Harrisburgh Advertiser), 1799-09-18, p.2].</ref>

The two issues repeat one list. Allegheny Township was then in Huntingdon County and later in Cambria County, so the county labels are compatible. The list does not establish a father-and-son relationship with a 1790 household head.

This may concern [[Glasgow-664]]. Profile exact birth 10 November 1777, Daill, Argyll, and death 21 May 1845, Glasgow, Cambria, Pennsylvania, fit the period. Its existing spouse has a profile-stated Huntingdon birthplace, a tree lead only; later Cambria locality and adult chronology make this a stronger regional candidate, without a direct connection to the township list.
